title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.834467: a fresh 2-cycle budget on metered fe_sub corrections

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.834467 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It keeps the kernels, step 69699/128 + 1155/256 + 25693/2^23 = 549.0382 instructions and correction account A (premise C, proof.md 5.4) of bradcush's 34a30cf5 (125.834643) and changes only the budget, the fresh 2-cycle budget: fresh 2-cycle catches (at most 805 milli-units each) leave the Markov allowance for a fixed row B_c = 0.805*(1 + 2^-40)*(S_int + 2^61)/(4R) units, R = 2^26. The disclosed premise P1, the conditional reading of H1's partition and twist fields, bounds the chance that a phase-1 arrival closes a fresh 2-cycle, given all computed before its point, by 1/(4R), 3/2 times the uniform 1/(6R); by Chernoff, more catches than B_c pays is a failure row below 10^-50. Premise P2 (at most 2^10 expected merging trails in phase 1) puts merged trails' catches in a 2^80-unit row. Pre-declared censuses on toy groups and on production secp256k1 at R = 2^16 support P1 (proof.md 5.5). The work bound uses none of C, P1 and P2. The declared run executes the shipped loops and arrival rows against big-integer secp256k1 with 0 mismatches, checks every returned borrow count, enters all 1,935 + 258 exit stubs and recomputes both census rules (evidence.md). R = 2^26, kappa = 1.0001, h = 0.0000116, p0 = 0.39001172. Declared dependencies (proof.md section 6): 34a30cf5, 0cd0ad73, 850e11fe, 886e6f54, a00774d8, c06f6691, 4ac17b66, 445f9a1c, cbea87bf, 4c8222cc, 0a1c5772, 5f1ae3ce, 4595bad7, 01488655, 2bd168b5, daf2c741, a9297fb0, 807e4bf5, b5de673a, 02feb284. Under H1, C, P1 and P2 the recovery probability is at least 0.39000001 > 0.39 (failure rows < 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory < 2^72 bytes; preprocessing capped at 2^59 units and included; no advice. Exact ledger: W_ledger < 2^125.8344669 units; Markov ratio at most 0.0000115354 (exact, rounded up) < 0.0000116; certificate.py checks the claim and that 125.834466 fails, in exact arithmetic. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule. Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the walk of proof.md 5.1 on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with node routing, and a check that the (1, 256) and production compare rules reach the same endpoints. Kernels (evidence.md items 1-9): limb ports against big integers; the shipped loops, both copies of loop A and the arrival rows run by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, big-integer dx and the exact canonical rule, every stub entered and every returned borrow count checked; counts and the ledger recomputed; both census rules recomputed from census-corr.json and census-p1.json, each with a run prefix re-walked. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^23 concurrent walks.
